[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Writing & Records[/color][/head]
Paper still runs the war. Orders, reports, passports and propaganda all move on physical documents, and a well-written page can be as powerful as a rifle. Writing is a core roleplay tool on Hullrot: Eclipsion, so use it.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Paper and pens[/color][/head]
- Pick up a sheet of [color=#6ab7d6]paper[/color] and use it with a [color=#6ab7d6]pen[/color] in hand to write on it. - Use a [color=#6ab7d6]stamp[/color] to mark a document as official, since orders, warrants, and rulings carry weight when properly stamped. - Write your text, then press [bold]Save[/bold] or [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="MultilineTextSubmit"/][/color]. Closing the window does [color=#d9776c]not[/color] save unsaved changes. Activate a document to read it; examining it only tells you that it contains writing or stamps.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Formatting[/color][/head]
You can use the same markup shown throughout this guidebook to make documents clear and official-looking. Wrap text in tags written inside square brackets.
- [color=#6ab7d6]\[head=2\]Field Report\[\/head\][/color] makes a heading. - [color=#6ab7d6]\[bold\]Important\[\/bold\][/color] emphasizes text. - [color=#6ab7d6]\[color=#e8b04b\]Warning\[\/color\][/color] colors text with a hex code.
Each tag is opened and then closed after the text it affects. Copy the examples above and replace only the visible words or color value.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]What to write[/color][/head]
- [bold]Orders and reports.[/bold] Commanders issue written orders and soldiers file after-action reports. A paper trail keeps a faction organized. - [bold]Propaganda.[/bold] The League and the Mandate both fight a war of ideas. Leaflets, manifestos, and declarations shape morale. - [bold]Identity and permits.[/bold] Passports, contracts, and permits define who a character is and what they are allowed to do. - [bold]Personal writing.[/bold] Journals, letters, and last words make characters feel real and give others something to discover.
[color=#6ab7d6]Tip:[/color] a stamped, signed, well-formatted document is far more convincing in-character than a scrawled note. If you want people to take your orders seriously, make them look official.
